title: Genie 4: Google's world model you steer with words
sources: https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-a-new-generation-of-world-simulation/ (DeepMind post and its demo videos, captured 2026-10-29)

segments.text: Google DeepMind just announced Genie 4, a world model that builds a scene from a prompt, then lets you walk around in it and steer it in real time.
Google's post about it already has over a million views.
The big idea is that you can use plain language to change the simulation while it's running, like changing the weather, moving the camera, or adding a new person.

shot.highlight: use natural language to modify a simulation in real-time

segments.text: So here's a man playing saxophone on a platform in a lake, and the text prompts steer the scene as it goes.
It's also much better at physics, things like collisions and aerodynamics.
Like this maple seed falling from the tree into the grass.
And here's Genie 3 next to Genie 4. The new one is far more photorealistic.
TechCrunch reports it can keep a scene consistent for up to two minutes, double what Genie 3 could do.

shot.highlight: It can maintain a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double its predecessor’s limit

segments.text: It's also their first real-time world model to generate audio natively: ambient sound, music, and even characters talking back.

shot.highlight: Genie 4 is our first real-time world model to generate audio natively

segments.text: Under the hood, Gemini acts as the director, planning the steps and checking frames while Genie makes the visuals.

shot.highlight: acting as the director that plans steps and checks frames while Genie creates the visuals

segments.text: For now it's a research preview for trusted testers, and it's coming to Google AI Ultra subscribers and the Gemini API next.

shot.highlight: We have started rolling Genie 4 out as a research preview for trusted testers
